questions.prompt: What are the two core functions of a **CPU (Central Processing Unit)**?

options.text: Fetching/decoding instructions and executing arithmetic, logic, and control operations

questions.prompt: Match each motherboard bus/interface to its primary role.

columns.label: High-speed lanes for GPUs, NVMe SSDs, and network cards
Serial storage interface for 2.5"/3.5" HDDs and SATA SSDs
System memory (RAM) modules connected to the CPU memory controller

questions.prompt: Why is **CPU cache (L1/L2/L3)** dramatically faster than main system RAM?

options.text: Cache has larger capacity than SSDs
Cache uses SRAM located directly on the CPU die, avoiding off-chip memory bus latency
Cache is stored on magnetic platters

questions.prompt: Which factors are key **CPU performance** characteristics? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Clock frequency and IPC (Instructions Per Clock)

questions.prompt: How does a **GPU** differ architecturally from a **CPU**?

options.text: GPUs have thousands of simpler cores optimized for massive data-parallel SIMD/SIMT throughput

questions.prompt: What is **VRAM** on a graphics card?

options.text: Virtual disk swap on an HDD
High-bandwidth memory dedicated to the GPU for framebuffers, textures, and compute tensors

questions.prompt: What does a **PSU (Power Supply Unit)** do?

options.text: Converts AC mains power into regulated DC voltage rails (+12V, +5V, +3.3V) for internal components

questions.prompt: What does an **80 PLUS** rating (Bronze, Gold, Platinum) on a PSU indicate?

options.text: Power conversion efficiency (less wasted heat at given load percentages)

questions.prompt: Which components are **non-volatile** storage (retaining data when power is off)? (Select all that apply.)
Which Linux command displays CPU architecture, core count, and cache sizes?
Why do **NVMe SSDs** outperform **SATA SSDs**?

options.text: NVMe connects directly over PCIe lanes with deep parallel command queues instead of the legacy SATA bottleneck

questions.prompt: In an **HDD (magnetic disk)**, what causes **seek time**?

options.text: Mechanical movement of the actuator arm and platter rotation to position the read/write head over a track/sector

questions.prompt: Match each I/O connector to its typical use.

columns.label: External peripherals, docks, and portable drives
Discrete graphics cards and high-speed accelerators

questions.prompt: What is **ECC (Error-Correcting Code) memory** used for in servers and workstations?

options.text: Detecting and correcting single-bit memory errors silently to prevent silent data corruption and crashes

questions.prompt: What is a **UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply)** used for in server rooms?

options.text: Providing short-term battery backup and surge conditioning so systems stay up or shut down cleanly during power loss

questions.prompt: Which practices protect **backup media** against ransomware and physical disasters? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Periodically testing restore speed and integrity
Storing the only backup on the same RAID array as production
Following the 3-2-1 rule (3 copies, 2 media types, 1 offsite/immutable)
Using air-gapped or immutable storage (e.g., WORM / offline tape)

questions.prompt: Why is **RAID** (e.g., RAID 1/5/6/10) NOT a substitute for backups?

options.text: RAID protects against disk hardware failure, NOT accidental deletes, corruption, or ransomware

questions.prompt: In **networking**, what does a **Layer 2 switch** use to forward frames within a LAN?
What does a **router** do that a basic Layer 2 switch does not?

options.text: Forwards IP packets between different networks/subnets using routing tables

questions.prompt: Which Linux command lists PCIe devices (GPUs, NVMe controllers, NICs)?
Which components belong in a **data center** physical infrastructure? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Hot-aisle / cold-aisle airflow and precision cooling
Redundant PDUs, UPS, and backup generators
Physical access control and environmental sensors

questions.prompt: What is **thermal throttling**?

options.text: A CPU or GPU automatically reducing clock speed when temperatures approach safe thermal limits

questions.prompt: Which command inspects block devices, partitions, and mount points on Linux?
Why do **server racks** use **redundant power supplies (dual PSUs)**?

options.text: So a single PSU or power-circuit failure does not take the server offline

questions.prompt: Match each storage tier to its primary trade-off.

columns.label: Lowest latency and highest IOPS, highest $/GB
Low $/GB for bulk sequential/warm storage, higher latency
Lowest $/TB for long-term archival and air-gapped offline retention

questions.prompt: What is **PCIe lane count** (e.g., x1, x4, x16)?

options.text: Number of parallel full-duplex serial links dedicated to a slot or device, determining peak bandwidth

questions.prompt: What does **SMART** monitoring on HDDs/SSDs report?

options.text: Drive health telemetry such as reallocated sectors, temperature, and wear-leveling indicators

questions.prompt: What is **fiber optic** cabling's advantage over copper Ethernet for long runs?

options.text: Higher bandwidth over much longer distances with immunity to electromagnetic interference (EMI)
It is cheaper for 1-meter patch cords

Which precautions prevent **ESD (Electrostatic Discharge)** damage when assembling hardware? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Using a grounded anti-static wrist strap
Touching a grounded metal chassis before handling bare PCBs
Rubbing wool socks on carpet before touching CPU pins

questions.prompt: What is **dual-channel / multi-channel memory**?

options.text: Populating matched DIMM slots across independent memory channels to multiply memory bandwidth

questions.prompt: What is **TDP (Thermal Design Power)**?

options.text: The maximum heat (in Watts) a cooling system must dissipate under sustained load

questions.prompt: What is the role of the **UEFI / BIOS** firmware on a motherboard?

options.text: Initializing hardware (POST), configuring low-level settings, and handing off boot to the OS bootloader

questions.prompt: Which command lists USB devices attached to a Linux host?
Why do enterprise servers use **hot-swap drive bays**?

options.text: To replace a failed drive in a RAID array without powering down the server

questions.prompt: What is **bandwidth** vs. **latency** in hardware interconnects?

options.text: Bandwidth is data rate (GB/s or Gbps); latency is delay for the first byte to arrive (ns or ms)

questions.prompt: Which factors determine **GPU suitability** for AI/HPC compute vs. basic display output? (Select all that apply.)
What does **PUE (Power Usage Effectiveness)** measure in a data center?

options.text: Total facility power divided by IT equipment power (closer to 1.0 means less cooling/overhead waste)

questions.prompt: Why should **PSU wattage** include headroom above peak component draw?

options.text: To handle transient power spikes, keep efficiency near the ~50-70% sweet spot, and reduce fan noise/heat

questions.prompt: What is **NIC teaming / link aggregation (LACP)**?

options.text: Bonding multiple physical network ports for higher aggregate throughput and link-level redundancy

questions.prompt: What is **IPMIs / BMC (Baseboard Management Controller)** used for in server hardware?

options.text: Out-of-band remote power control, sensor telemetry, and console access even when the OS is down
